--- stdout ---
- Never assume, verify before claiming
- List development targets with `make help`
- Read relevant developer documentation in the `docs` folder
- PR descriptions: minimal, only what and why, no task or file listings. Include screenshots for UI changes, before and after when modifying existing UI. Aim for less than 1000 characters
- Reference issues and PRs by full URL, not by number
- Use Conventional Commits for commit messages and PR titles, plus Gitea's `enhance` type for user-facing enhancements
- Add an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer to commit messages, never `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by`
- Attribute agent authorship on one trailing line in issue and PR comments, never as a PR description section
- Never rewrite git history unless asked, update PRs with new commits and normal push
- Comments: write almost none, short and preferably same-line, explaining why for a future reader. Never narrate code, the change or the prompt. Preserve existing ones that still apply. If you need to write a paragraph-long comment, rethink your implementation, it is likely too complicated
- Add the current year to copyright headers of new `.go` files
- In `options/locale`, only edit `locale_en-US.json`, other locales are synced automatically
- In TS, use `!` instead of `?.`/`??` when a value always exists
- In Go, prefer to use modern language features wherever possible
- Write sizes as multiplications like `64 * 1024`, not bit shifts like `64 << 10`
- Prefer `tw-*` utilities over inline `style` and `flex-*` helpers over per-child `tw-ml-*`/`tw-mr-*` margins, falling back to `tw-*` where specificity requires `!important`
- Run `make fmt` after `.go` edits, `make tidy` after `go.mod` edits, `make generate-swagger` after API changes, and lint what changed with `make lint-go`, `lint-js`, `lint-css` or `lint-templates`
- Fix the cause rather than disabling a linter or weakening a test. Where unavoidable, use the narrowest scope with a trailing comment giving the reason
- Run single tests with `go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/` for Go, `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` for TS and `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e` for e2e
- Write the fewest, fastest tests covering the behavior, extending an existing one where possible. Prefer unit tests where logic is testable in isolation
- Aim for sub-2s per integration test and sub-4s per e2e test. Wait on a deterministic condition rather than `sleep`, and prefer semantic locators in e2e tests

commit 0964106988bb430ad5f1a2ec2a36431421811fc7
Author: silverwind <me@silverwind.io>
Date:   Fri Oct 30 08:08:32 2026 +0100

    fix: add missing access checks and size limits (#39942) (#40085)
    
    Backport https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/39942
    
    Several handlers and parsers skipped checks that their siblings already
    perform.
    
    - Reject issue, comment, label, milestone and release mutations in
    archived repositories via the API with one guard per route group,
    matching the web UI
    - Hide timeline references and dependencies pointing at issues the doer
    cannot read, in the web UI and the API, including pull requests of the
    same repository without pull request access
    - Reject workflow runs with more than `MaxJobNumPerRun` jobs, including
    inline reusable workflow jobs, and show rejected pushes as invalid
    workflow runs
    - Bound how much of a Helm chart archive is inflated while looking for
    `Chart.yaml`
    
    `release/v28` lacks two helpers this needs, so they are included:
    `insertInvalidWorkflowRun`, split out of `handleInvalidWorkflows` by
    https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/39480, and
    `packages.NewLimitedReader` from
    https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/39366.
    
    Co-authored-by: bircni <bircni@icloud.com>
    Co-authored-by: wxiaoguang <wxiaoguang@gmail.com>

content.text:
I fixed the 20 advisories OSV reported against this Gitea checkout by cherry-picking the upstream fix commits that are already in the local git object store. Builds, `go vet`, unit tests and the relevant integration tests pass. I did not re-run `osv_scan`, which flags the checkout by commit hash, so it will keep listing them until the changes are committed. I did not start the app and exercise it by hand, and `run_tests` only ran `./modules/markup/...`, so I ran the Go tests myself.

**What was wrong:** OSV's only findings were Gitea's own advisories, all marked fixed in 28.3.0. There were no dependency CVEs. A full upgrade would have pulled in about 60 unrelated commits, so I took only the fixes for these CVEs.

**What I applied:** I cherry-picked these seven fix commits without committing them, so the 51 changed files are staged in the working tree. I left the commit to you.

| Commit | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ef2ceff6cd` | Actions v1 artifact `Content-Encoding` XSS |
| `01db50f0bf` | `public-only` token scope bypasses (heatmap, runner registration, admin API, profiles, packages, OAuth userinfo, repo and org creation, bulk delete) |
| `0964106988` | Archived-repo API mutations, issue dependency disclosure, Helm decompression limit |
| `5ba69f9af4` | Fork workflow trust on review-triggered runs |
| `5a3f06430d` | System users owning nothing: task-token repo enumeration, commit-signing spoof, feed scope |
| `a1c56dd96a` | Private pull requests shown on project boards |
| `dfdb0438ad` | OAuth2 auto-link account takeover |

**One conflict:** `0964106988` conflicted in `services/migrations/onedev.go` and its test. That code is a OneDev migration cleanup unrelated to the CVEs, so I kept the existing versions of both files.

**Checks:**
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` on the affected packages are clean, and `gofmt` reports nothing.
- Unit tests pass in all 23 affected non-integration packages.
- The sqlite integration tests covering the changed areas pass (artifacts, heatmap, feeds, OAuth2 link signup, issue dependencies, archived-repo mutations, public-only tokens, projects, Actions permissions and triggers, issue API).
